title: Orbital Embedding and the Physical Definition of Quantum Geometry
abstract: The Quantum Geometric Tensor, encompassing the quantum metric and Berry curvature, is a central concept in modern condensed matter physics. However, its standard calculation via $k$-derivatives of the Bloch projector conceals a fundamental ambiguity regarding the choice of unit-cell convention, specifically in the treatment of intra-cell orbital positions (i.e., with or without the orbital position $e^{ikx_α}$). We resolve this inconsistency by introducing a convention-independent physical QGT defined via a covariant derivative that explicitly incorporates the full position operator. We demonstrate that this formulation is uniquely mandated by the microscopic derivation of the physical current via the Peierls substitution. Notably, we uncover a leading-order failure in standard $k \cdot p$ effective theories for systems with bond-ordered gaps, identifying a need for caution in their application. Finally, we propose geometric engineering as a new design paradigm, enabling the independent tuning of geometric responses without altering the energy dispersion.
summary: This work resolves a fundamental ambiguity in calculating the Quantum Geometric Tensor by proposing a physically mandated definition using a covariant derivative that includes the full orbital position operator. The authors demonstrate that ignoring this embedding leads to unphysical results, particularly in low-energy effective theories near gapped regimes.
main_problem: The standard calculation of the Quantum Geometric Tensor (QGT) suffers from an ambiguity dependent on the choice of unit-cell convention when dealing with Bloch states and $k$-derivatives.
main_result: A physically mandated, convention-independent QGT must be defined using a covariant derivative that explicitly incorporates the full position operator, revealing leading-order failures in standard k.p effective theories for gapped systems.
method: The authors introduce a covariant derivative $D_\mu = i[\cdot, \hat{r}_\mu]$ to define a physical QGT, contrasting it with conventional $k$-derivative approaches.
model_or_system: The analysis uses general condensed matter models, specifically demonstrating the issue using the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model and a one-dimensional massive Dirac Hamiltonian.

figures_summary: Figures compare results for SSH models and Dirac Hamiltonians, showing that convention A leads to unphysical asymmetries in observables like conductivity, while convention B restores necessary symmetries.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the ambiguity in QGT calculation; it then uses the SSH model to demonstrate the failure of standard derivatives; subsequently, it analyzes gapped effective theories using the Dirac Hamiltonian to show that orbital embedding corrections are essential for accurate physical responses.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state theory, the concept of defining observables via covariant derivatives incorporating full position operators is a general mathematical tool applicable to open quantum systems where boundary conditions or spatial degrees of freedom must be rigorously accounted for.
